entry.title: Dr. Zhang accepted into the MADRC Early Career Investigator Mentorship Program

link.title: Dr. Zhang accepted into the MADRC Early Career Investigator Mentorship Program

entry.content: Dr. Zhang has been selected as a awardee in the Michigan Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center (MADRC) Early Career Investigator Mentorship Program, supported by a P30 grant from the National Institutes on Aging. This two-year support will expand his current research program in vascular physiology and healthy aging and strategically position his research to address cerebrovascular contributions to Alzheimer’s disease.

entry.title: Liu and Zhang labs awarded a NIH Trailblazer R21 grant

link.title: Liu and Zhang labs awarded a NIH Trailblazer R21 grant

entry.content: The Liu Lab in Department of Chemical Engineering & Materials Science and the Zhang Lab in Department of Physiology received a mutliple-PI Trailblazer R21 award from the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering (NIBIB) to develop a flexible, biocompatible optical fiber for efficient calcium signal detection in skeletal muscles of awake, free behaving animals. This technology and collaboration will expand our ability to investigate the physiological mechanisms that link activity in the brain and body.

entry.title: Lab trainees honored at Department of Physiology annual retreat

link.title: Lab trainees honored at Department of Physiology annual retreat

entry.content:
Olivia Morris, a second year graduate student in Molecular, Cellular, and Integrative Physiology, was invited to give a trainee talk at our department’s annual retreat and received the First Place Award for her poster presentation in graduate student division.
Fellow lab member, Joslyn Claypool, received the Second Place Award for her poster presentation in undergraduate student division, another big accomplishment before beginning her graduate school journey at UMass Chan Medical School.
Congratulations, Olivia and Joslyn!

entry.title: Jaini awarded two prestigious MSU fellowships

link.title: Jaini awarded two prestigious MSU fellowships

entry.content:
Jaini Gandhi, a senior majoring in neuroscience and an undergraduate research assistant in our lab, recently won two prestigious fellowships to support her summer research and senior thesis work: the Hymen and Miriam Stein Scholarship from Honors College at Michigan State University and the Larry D. Fowler Endowment Undergraduate Research Scholarship from College of Natural Science at Michigan State University.
Jaini will be working on optimizing pupil tracking algorithms and investigating the neurophysiology underlying motivated behaviors.
Congratulations, Jaini!

entry.title: Zhang Lab awarded a Bridge Career Development Award from AHA

link.title: Zhang Lab awarded a Bridge Career Development Award from AHA

entry.content: The Zhang Lab received a Bridge Career Development Award from American Heart Association to continue the work investigating structural and functional changes of cerebral microcirculation in healthy aging, with a special focus on astrocyte-mediated cerebrovascular control.

entry.title: Dual fellowships support Joslyn’s deep dive into neurophysiology

link.title: Dual fellowships support Joslyn’s deep dive into neurophysiology

entry.content:
Joslyn will use our widefield fluorescence optical imaging system and fiber photometry system to understand how adenosine plays a role in brain hemodynamics regulation. Image credit: Tyler Lee.

Joslyn Claypool, an undergraduate research assistant in our lab, recently won two prestigious awards: the 2025 Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship from the American Physiological Society (one of the 12 students internationally) and a research support fellowship from MSU’s College of Natural Science. A double major in neuroscience and psychology, Joslyn is investigating how adenosine, a chemical affected by caffeine, influences brain blood flow and inflammation. To learn more about Joslyn and her research , please read the Student Spotlight article posted by our departmental communication team. Congratulations, Joslyn!
